scientific_queries.note: Minimal-evidence question answered against the marginal baseline established in R70-R75.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round re-asks an old question against the newly established strong baseline and finds that small amounts of personal data are harmful.

design.baseline: drug pair marginals estimated from training cells only; the held-out cell contributes nothing
design.personal_arm: estimate cell-specific drug residuals from m measured rows and add them to the marginal score
design.metric: hit rate at k=20 on the UNMEASURED remainder of the cell's pool

headline: below about 50 measured combinations a new cell's own data makes decisions WORSE (m=10: -1.59 pp, m=25: -1.23 pp, both CIs exclude zero); the crossover is near 50 and significance arrives at m=100 (+1.64 pp), with m=200 best at +2.62 pp
mechanism_reading: with few measurements each drug gets less than one or two data points, so the estimated residual is noise that perturbs an otherwise correct marginal ranking
relation_to_R22: R22 showed pooling was already near the ceiling but did not show that too little personal data is actively harmful; this round supplies the cost curve
limits: the m=400 arm has only 960 observations because many cell pools are too small, so its non-monotonicity is a sample effect
the personal arm's estimator (per-drug residual mean) is one reasonable construction; other constructions may shift the threshold
drug marginals come from training cells only, which keeps the baseline clean
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: test whether the threshold scales with the cell's pool size, which would turn the fixed 100 into a proportion

register_updates.C50: new, exploratory: minimal personal evidence is about 100 measurements, and below 50 it is harmful
register_updates.SYNTHESIS: a row added to the evidence table
